subject: General Knowledge
topic: Books and authors III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The book 'The Discovery of India', which surveys India's history and civilisation from the Indus Valley period to the eve of independence, was authored by which Indian statesman?

options.option_text: Subhas Chandra Bose, leader of the Indian National Army
Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister
Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the 'Iron Man of India'

questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' (1946) while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort during 1942–46. It traces India's philosophical, cultural, and political history. Rajendra Prasad, a common distractor, authored 'India Divided' — a different work on Partition.

questions.stem: The memoir 'India Wins Freedom', which recounts the events surrounding Indian independence and Partition from an insider's perspective, was written by which leader?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, who served as the first Prime Minister
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, India's first Education Minister
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, known as the Iron Man of India
C. Rajagopalachari, the last Governor-General of India

questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad authored 'India Wins Freedom' (1959). Notably, 30 pages were kept sealed for 30 years as per his wish and published only in 1988. Nehru is a common wrong pick; his comparable memoir-style work is 'The Discovery of India'.

questions.stem: 'Rajatarangini', a Sanskrit historical chronicle recording the succession of Kashmir's kings from mythological origins to the 12th century CE, was composed by which scholar?

options.option_text: Banabhatta, the court poet of Emperor Harsha of Thanesar
Somadeva, who compiled the Kathasaritsagara in Sanskrit verse
Kalhana, a Kashmiri poet who wrote in the 12th century CE
Jayadeva, the author of the devotional poem Gita Govinda

questions.explanation: 'Rajatarangini' (River of Kings, c. 1148–1150 CE) was composed by Kalhana, a Kashmiri Brahmin scholar — it is considered India's earliest systematic historical chronicle. Somadeva (Kathasaritsagara) and Banabhatta (Harshacharita) are plausible distractors but belong to different works and regions.

questions.stem: 'Indica', the earliest firsthand Greek account describing Mauryan India's social hierarchy, urban planning, and royal administration, was authored by whom?

options.option_text: Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya's court
Ptolemy, the Greco-Egyptian astronomer and mathematical geographer
Fa Hien, a Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who toured India's monasteries
Hiuen Tsang, who travelled across India during the reign of Harsha

questions.explanation: Megasthenes served as a Seleucid ambassador at the Mauryan court in Pataliputra (c. 302 BCE) and wrote 'Indica', now known only through later citations. Fa Hien and Hiuen Tsang are frequent wrong answers because they also wrote India accounts, but they were Chinese pilgrims of the Gupta and Harsha eras respectively.

questions.stem: Gandhi's political tract 'Hind Swaraj' (1909), which argued for rejection of Western industrial civilisation and passive resistance, was originally composed in which language?

options.option_text: Hindi, the lingua franca of the northern Indian heartland
English, the administrative language of the colonial government
Gujarati, Gandhi's own mother tongue and the original manuscript
Marathi, the dominant language of the Deccan plateau region

questions.explanation: Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj' in Gujarati aboard a ship returning from London in 1909 and translated it into English himself. The British government banned the English translation; the Gujarati original was left untouched. Many candidates assume it was written in Hindi or English, making Gujarati a high-value recall point.

questions.stem: 'Ghulamgiri' (1873), which drew an explicit parallel between the plight of oppressed castes in India and the enslavement of Black people in America and was dedicated to 'the good people of the United States', was authored by which reformer?

options.option_text: B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution
E.V. Ramasamy Periyar, founder of the Self-Respect Movement
Narayana Guru, a spiritual and social reformer from Kerala
Jyotirao Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873

questions.explanation: Jyotirao Phule wrote 'Ghulamgiri' (Slavery) in Marathi in 1873, the same year he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj. The America-slavery parallel is distinctive. Ambedkar is the most tempting distractor because he is more widely associated with anti-caste writing, but his landmark works ('Annihilation of Caste', 1936) came decades later.

questions.stem: The 'Ashtadhyayi', a Sanskrit grammatical treatise consisting of approximately 3,959 sutras arranged into eight chapters and considered the world's first generative grammar, was composed by which ancient scholar?

options.option_text: Panini, the ancient grammarian from the Gandhara region
Patanjali, who composed the 'Mahabhashya' on Sanskrit grammar
Bhartrhari, who authored the 'Vakyapadiya' on linguistic theory
Katyayana, who wrote the 'Varttikas' as supplements to grammar

questions.explanation: Panini (c. 4th century BCE), from Shalatula in the Gandhara region, composed the 'Ashtadhyayi' — a highly systematic grammar of Classical Sanskrit. Patanjali (Mahabhashya) and Katyayana (Varttikas) both commented on Panini's work; Bhartrhari analysed sentence meaning. Candidates confuse Patanjali (grammarian) with Patanjali (Yoga Sutras author), making all three distractors genuinely plausible.
